_comment: Canonical factors for the system map. Claims use the names in `name`; any claim factor listed in `aliases` is merged into that factor when the model is built. column is an editorial framing (pressure, structure, people, outcome): causes generally sit left and results right. valence -1 marks factors that are bad when they grow (used to flag mixed effects). Edit freely; then run `yarn system-map:build`.

factors.name: financial pressure
factors.definition: Cost, cash and margin strain on the organization.

factors.name: competition
factors.definition: Rival plans, systems and models competing for members and physicians.

factors.name: rapid change
factors.definition: Fast-moving shifts in health care, technology or organization that outpace adjustment.

factors.name: secrecy
factors.definition: Decisions made or announced without consulting those affected.

factors.name: data & technology
factors.definition: Electronic records, data systems, analytics, virtual care and AI.

factors.name: physician turnover
factors.definition: Physicians leaving, retiring early or not staying.

factors.name: fee-for-service
factors.definition: Payment by volume of services, and the incentives it creates.

factors.name: mandatory retirement
factors.definition: Required retirement at a set age.

factors.name: network expansion
factors.definition: Growth through contracted networks, the KP Medical Foundation, Risant and new markets rather than Permanente groups.

factors.name: contracted hospitals & providers
factors.definition: Relying on community hospitals and outside providers instead of KP-owned facilities and Permanente physicians.

factors.name: choice products
factors.definition: Benefit designs such as point-of-service, choice and high-deductible products.

factors.name: outside executives
factors.definition: Leaders recruited from outside KP who bring other industries' frames.

factors.name: health policy
factors.definition: Public policy and regulation such as the Affordable Care Act.

factors.name: labor support
factors.definition: Support from unions and employer groups that brought members.

factors.name: low pricing
factors.definition: Pricing premiums below cost to win or hold members.

factors.name: hospital divestiture
factors.definition: Selling or giving up owned hospitals.

factors.name: partnership with health plan
factors.definition: The mutual, exclusive partnership between the Permanente Medical Groups and the Health Plan and Hospitals.

factors.name: group practice
factors.definition: Multispecialty physicians practicing together as one salaried group.

factors.name: integrated care
factors.definition: Coverage, care and facilities joined in one system with shared incentives.

factors.name: physician leadership
factors.definition: Physicians leading the care system, including dyad partnerships with administrators.

factors.name: medical group autonomy
factors.definition: Each Permanente Medical Group governing itself independently.

factors.name: permanente federation
factors.definition: The national Federation that lets the medical groups act together, and its agreements with the Health Plan (e.g. Tahoe).

factors.name: medical group affiliation
factors.definition: Affiliations between Permanente groups, such as TPMG supporting Mid-Atlantic.

factors.name: capitation
factors.definition: Prepaid, per-member payment that rewards keeping people healthy.

factors.name: physician compensation
factors.definition: How physicians are paid: incentives, bonuses, deferred compensation.

factors.name: succession
factors.definition: Planned transfer of leadership to the next generation.

factors.name: best practice spread
factors.definition: Sharing proven practices across regions, e.g. through the Care Management Institute or shared services.

factors.name: research & education
factors.definition: Research units, teaching and medical education.

factors.name: nonprofit status
factors.definition: KP's nonprofit structure.

factors.name: decision-making
factors.definition: How quickly and clearly decisions get made, including role clarity.

factors.name: culture
factors.definition: Shared values, mission and ways of working, and the history behind them.

factors.name: trust
factors.definition: Confidence between physicians, leaders, the plan and patients.

factors.name: candor
factors.definition: Open, transparent communication, including admitting what isn't known.

factors.name: leadership development
factors.definition: Mentoring, training and growing physician leaders.

factors.name: physician well-being
factors.definition: Physicians' satisfaction, morale and sustainable workload.

factors.name: burnout
factors.definition: Physician exhaustion and overload.

factors.name: physician engagement
factors.definition: Physicians' buy-in to and involvement in organizational change.

factors.name: physician recruitment
factors.definition: Attracting and hiring physicians.

factors.name: clinical excellence
factors.definition: Physicians' clinical skill and credibility.

factors.name: equity
factors.definition: Fair care and outcomes across populations; addressing disparities.

factors.name: workforce diversity
factors.definition: Diversity of physicians and leaders.

factors.name: community health
factors.definition: Health of the wider community, including volunteering and pandemic response.

factors.name: quality
factors.definition: Clinical quality, safety and outcomes of care.

factors.name: affordability
factors.definition: Cost of care to members, employers and the organization.

factors.name: prevention
factors.definition: Preventive care and keeping members healthy.

factors.name: patient experience
factors.definition: Patients' and members' experience of care and service.

factors.name: access
factors.definition: Members' ability to get care when they need it.

factors.name: membership growth
factors.definition: Gaining and keeping members.

factors.name: innovation
factors.definition: New models, practices and the ability to adapt.

factors.name: organizational performance
factors.definition: Overall success and performance of the organization or medical group.

factors.name: brand & reputation
factors.definition: How KP and Permanente are seen by the public and the market.

factors.name: negotiating leverage
factors.definition: Bargaining power in negotiations.
